/-!
# Conjecture 1.35

by M. I. Kargapolov

Part c) (A. I. Mal'cev, L. Fuchs). Do there exist simple pro-orderable groups?
A group is said to be *pro-orderable* if each of its partial orderings can be
extended to a linear ordering.

Here a *partial ordering* (resp. *linear ordering*) of a group $G$ is a partial
(resp. linear) order $\le$ on $G$ that is compatible with the group operation on
both sides, i.e. $a \le b$ implies $x a y \le x b y$ for all $x, y \in G$. A linear
ordering $\preceq$ *extends* a partial ordering $\le$ if $a \le b$ implies
$a \preceq b$. Pro-orderable groups are also known as $O^*$-groups.

Only part c) of Problem 1.35 is formalised here; it is the only part that is
still open.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b x y : G, r a b → r (x * a * y) (x * b * y)
blocks.docstring:
A binary relation $r$ on a group $G$ is *bi-invariant* if $r(a, b)$ implies
$r(x a y, x b y)$ for all $x, y \in G$. A partial (resp. linear) ordering *of the
group* $G$ is a bi-invariant partial (resp. linear) order on $G$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«1.35».IsBiInvariant
justification.why_needed: 'Partial/linear ordering of a group' means an order compatible with multiplication on both sides (a ≤ b ⇒ x a y ≤ x b y). Mathlib only has this as typeclasses `MulLeftMono`/`MulRightMono` over a bundled `LE` instance; quantifying over orders as explicit relations `r : G → G → Prop` needs a relation-level predicate. An API lemma `isBiInvariant_le_iff` proves it is equivalent to `MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G` for the `≤` of any `LE G`.

blocks.name: IsBiInvariant
blocks.text:
/--
A binary relation $r$ on a group $G$ is *bi-invariant* if $r(a, b)$ implies
$r(x a y, x b y)$ for all $x, y \in G$. A partial (resp. linear) ordering *of the
group* $G$ is a bi-invariant partial (resp. linear) order on $G$.
-/
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b x y : G, r a b → r (x * a * y) (x * b * y)

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *pro-orderable* if each of its partial orderings can be extended to
a linear ordering. That is, for every bi-invariant partial order $\le$ on $G$ there
is a bi-invariant linear order $\preceq$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies
$a \preceq b$ for all $a, b \in G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No existing notion of orderable / bi-orderable / O*-group found (rg over Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for 'orderable', 'bi-invariant', 'LeftOrdered', 'BiOrdered').
justification.name: Kourovka.«1.35».IsProOrderable
justification.why_needed: The notebook's notion 'pro-orderable' (Mal'cev–Fuchs O*-group: every partial ordering of the group extends to a linear ordering of the group) does not exist in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Defined as: ∀ r, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant r → ∃ s, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s ∧ ∀ a b, r a b → s a b. Includes test `isProOrderable_unit` and API lemma `IsProOrderable.exists_isLinearOrder` (pro-orderable ⇒ orderable, via the trivial partial order).

blocks.name: IsProOrderable
blocks.text:
/--
A group $G$ is *pro-orderable* if each of its partial orderings can be extended to
a linear ordering. That is, for every bi-invariant partial order $\le$ on $G$ there
is a bi-invariant linear order $\preceq$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies
$a \preceq b$ for all $a, b \in G$.
-/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s ∧ ∀ a b : G, r a b → s a b

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem isBiInvariant_le_iff [LE G] :
    IsBiInvariant (G := G) (· ≤ ·) ↔ MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨⟨fun x a b hab => ?_⟩, ⟨fun x a b hab => ?_⟩⟩,
    fun ⟨hl, hr⟩ a b x y hab => ?_⟩
  · simpa using h a b x 1 hab
  · simpa using h a b 1 x hab
  · exact mul_le_mul_left (mul_le_mul_right hab x) y
blocks.docstring:
For an order `≤` on a group, bi-invariance is the same as the conjunction of Mathlib's
`MulLeftMono` and `MulRightMono`.

@[category test, AMS 6 20]
theorem isProOrderable_unit : IsProOrderable Unit :=
  fun _ _ _ => ⟨fun _ _ => True,
    { refl := fun _ => trivial
      trans := fun _ _ _ _ _ => trivial
      antisymm := fun a b _ _ => Subsingleton.elim a b
      total := fun _ _ => Or.inl trivial },
    fun _ _ _ _ _ => trivial, fun _ _ _ => trivial⟩

@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.exists_isLinearOrder (h : IsProOrderable G) :
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hs', -⟩ := h (· = ·)
    { refl := fun _ => rfl
      trans := fun _ _ _ h₁ h₂ => h₁.trans h₂
      antisymm := fun _ _ h₁ _ => h₁ }
    (fun _ _ _ _ hab => by rw [hab])
  exact ⟨s, hs, hs'⟩

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence question (the only still-open lettered part c), not starred as solved): 'partial ordering'/'linear ordering' of a group means a bi-invariant (a ≤ b ⇒ xay ≤ xby) partial/total order, so for noncommutative G one needs unbundled MulLeftMono ∧ MulRightMono (or an explicit relation) rather than IsOrderedMonoid, and 'simple' should be Mathlib's IsSimpleGroup (nontrivial) so the trivial group is not a degenerate witness; finite simple groups are automatically excluded since a pro-orderable group is orderable, hence torsion-free.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same, faithful content: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G : Type with Group G, IsSimpleGroup G (nontrivial, so the trivial group is excluded) ∧ every bi-invariant (a ≤ b ⇒ xay ≤ xby) partial order relation on G is contained in some bi-invariant total order relation on G. This matches the Fuchs/Mal'cev meaning of 'partial/linear ordering of a group' and 'extends' as relation inclusion. c04 was chosen because it follows the repository conventions (theorem name `kourovka.«1.35».parts.c` inside `namespace Kourovka.«1.35»`, witness in `Type` as in 1_40/1_74/19_25), factors the notion into two small bespoke definitions (`IsBiInvariant`, `IsProOrderable`) built on Mathlib's unbundled `IsPartialOrder`/`IsLinearOrder`, and supplies the API/test lemmas that CONTRIBUTING.md asks for — including `isBiInvariant_le_iff`, which checks the bespoke invariance against Mathlib's `MulLeftMono ∧ MulRightMono` exactly as the decomposition notes suggest, plus 'pro-orderable ⇒ orderable' and 'the trivial group is pro-orderable'. c01/c02/c06 inline the definition (fine but no API tests; c01 uses a non-conventional theorem name); c03 has an odd name `IsProorderable` and no tests; c05/c08 are equivalent to c04 with three definitions instead of two; c07 uses bundled `PartialOrder`/`LinearOrder` structures (classically equivalent but carries decidability data). File taken from c04 unchanged; compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.35

by M. I. Kargapolov

Part c) (A. I. Mal'cev, L. Fuchs). Do there exist simple pro-orderable groups?
A group is said to be *pro-orderable* if each of its partial orderings can be
extended to a linear ordering.

Here a *partial ordering* (resp. *linear ordering*) of a group $G$ is a partial
(resp. linear) order $\le$ on $G$ that is compatible with the group operation on
both sides, i.e. $a \le b$ implies $x a y \le x b y$ for all $x, y \in G$. A linear
ordering $\preceq$ *extends* a partial ordering $\le$ if $a \le b$ implies
$a \preceq b$. Pro-orderable groups are also known as $O^*$-groups.

Only part c) of Problem 1.35 is formalised here; it is the only part that is
still open.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.35»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/--
A binary relation $r$ on a group $G$ is *bi-invariant* if $r(a, b)$ implies
$r(x a y, x b y)$ for all $x, y \in G$. A partial (resp. linear) ordering *of the
group* $G$ is a bi-invariant partial (resp. linear) order on $G$.
-/
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b x y : G, r a b → r (x * a * y) (x * b * y)

/--
A group $G$ is *pro-orderable* if each of its partial orderings can be extended to
a linear ordering. That is, for every bi-invariant partial order $\le$ on $G$ there
is a bi-invariant linear order $\preceq$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies
$a \preceq b$ for all $a, b \in G$.
-/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s ∧ ∀ a b : G, r a b → s a b

/-- For an order `≤` on a group, bi-invariance is the same as the conjunction of Mathlib's
`MulLeftMono` and `MulRightMono`. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem isBiInvariant_le_iff [LE G] :
    IsBiInvariant (G := G) (· ≤ ·) ↔ MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨⟨fun x a b hab => ?_⟩, ⟨fun x a b hab => ?_⟩⟩,
    fun ⟨hl, hr⟩ a b x y hab => ?_⟩
  · simpa using h a b x 1 hab
  · simpa using h a b 1 x hab
  · exact mul_le_mul_left (mul_le_mul_right hab x) y

/-- The trivial group is pro-orderable. -/
@[category test, AMS 6 20]
theorem isProOrderable_unit : IsProOrderable Unit :=
  fun _ _ _ => ⟨fun _ _ => True,
    { refl := fun _ => trivial
      trans := fun _ _ _ _ _ => trivial
      antisymm := fun a b _ _ => Subsingleton.elim a b
      total := fun _ _ => Or.inl trivial },
    fun _ _ _ _ _ => trivial, fun _ _ _ => trivial⟩

/-- A pro-orderable group is orderable: applying the definition to the trivial partial
ordering (equality) yields a linear ordering of the group. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.exists_isLinearOrder (h : IsProOrderable G) :
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hs', -⟩ := h (· = ·)
    { refl := fun _ => rfl
      trans := fun _ _ _ h₁ h₂ => h₁.trans h₂
      antisymm := fun _ _ h₁ _ => h₁ }
    (fun _ _ _ _ hab => by rw [hab])
  exact ⟨s, hs, hs'⟩

/--
(A. I. Mal'cev, L. Fuchs). Do there exist simple pro-orderable groups? A group is said
to be *pro-orderable* if each of its partial orderings can be extended to a linear
ordering.

Here "simple" is in the usual group-theoretic sense (`IsSimpleGroup`): the group is
nontrivial and has no normal subgroups other than the trivial subgroup and the whole
group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.35».parts.c : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsSimpleGroup G ∧ IsProOrderable G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.35»

items: Group orderings are two-sided (bi-)invariant: `IsBiInvariant r := ∀ a b x y, r a b → r (x*a*y) (x*b*y)`. This is the standard Fuchs/Mal'cev/Kokorin–Kopytov meaning of a 'partially ordered group'; one-sided invariance was not intended by the source.

Orders are quantified as explicit relations `r : G → G → Prop` with Mathlib's `IsPartialOrder`/`IsLinearOrder`, rather than bundled `PartialOrder G`/`LinearOrder G` instances. A first draft with bundled instances and `letI` was rejected because Lean silently resolved the `LE` instance for the linear order to the bound partial-order variable (both were local instances), which would have misformalized the statement.
'Extends' means containment of relations: `∀ a b, r a b → s a b`.

The trivial partial order (equality) counts as a partial ordering, so a pro-orderable group is in particular (bi-)orderable, hence torsion-free; this matches the standard definition of O*-groups and is recorded by the API lemma `IsProOrderable.exists_isLinearOrder`.
'Simple' is Mathlib's `IsSimpleGroup` (which includes `Nontrivial`), so the trivial group is not a degenerate witness.
The witness group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the other Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25).
AMS tags 6 (ordered algebraic structures) and 20 (group theory).
The module docstring states that part c) is the only part of Problem 1.35 still open, following the task's decomposition notes; parts a) and b) are not formalized.

reviewer_notes: Interpretation points: (1) 'partial ordering'/'linear ordering' of a group are read as two-sided invariant orders (standard in Fuchs, Kokorin–Kopytov; pro-orderable groups = O*-groups); all candidates agreed. (2) 'Extends' = relation inclusion. (3) 'Simple' = Mathlib `IsSimpleGroup` (includes Nontrivial); since equality is a bi-invariant partial order, pro-orderable ⇒ bi-orderable ⇒ torsion-free, so finite simple groups are automatically excluded without extra hypotheses. (4) Witness quantified over `Type` (universe 0) following the existing Kourovka files. No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition table were raised, and I found none.
